messages.text: Hamilton: Ferrari have to catch up with rivals on power

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton is urging Ferrari to improve the performance of their power unit for the 2027 Formula 1 season as the 41-year-old eyes a shot at a record eighth world championship next year.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton insists Ferrari must 'catch up' with rivals on power unit performance for 2027 F1 season | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton insists Ferrari must 'catch up' with rivals on power unit performance for 2027 F1 season Lewis Hamilton has dropped more than 100 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli amid Ferrari's inability to match Mercedes' power; watch F1's first ever Singapore Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1, with Sprint Qualifying at 1pm on Friday Wednesday 7 October 2026 07:00, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reveals his heart sank when Ferrari chose to start on soft tyres while the majority of other cars started on intermediates Lewis Hamilton is urging Ferrari to improve the performance of their power unit for the 2027 Formula 1 season as the 41-year-old eyes a shot at a record eighth world championship next year. A first Ferrari grand prix victory for Hamilton in Barcelona in June provided hope that he could launch a 2026 title challenge, but an underwhelming run after the summer break saw his deficit to Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli grow beyond 100 points. Hamilton ended a streak of six races without a podium by finishing third at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday, with only a poor choice of starting tyre costing him the chance to use his impressive pace to battle Red Bull's Max Verstappen for victory. messages.text: 'No excuses' for Reed after injury as he looks to increase Race to Dubai lead

metadata.summary: Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed says becoming the second American to be crowned European No 1 would mean "a lot" and insists he has "no excuses" as he looks to extend his advantage over Rory McIlroy after returning from a shoulder injury.
metadata.content: Open de Espana: Patrick Reed looking to extend lead over Rory McIlroy in Race to Dubai as he makes return from injury | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Open de Espana: Patrick Reed looking to extend lead over Rory McIlroy in Race to Dubai as he makes return from injury Patrick Reed around 300 points clear of Rory McIlroy in Race to Dubai as he looks to become second American to be crowned European No 1; Reed hopes his success will encourage his countrymen to play more worldwide; watch Open de Espana live on Sky Sports from 1pm Thursday Wednesday 7 October 2026 07:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' golf pundits discuss whether more American stars like Scottie Scheffler should play on the DP World Tour? Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed says becoming the second American to be crowned European No 1 would mean "a lot" and insists he has "no excuses" as he looks to extend his advantage over Rory McIlroy after returning from a shoulder injury. Reed will tee it up at the Open de Espana from Thursday in his first appearance since withdrawing during the second round of the flagship BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth last month. The 36-year-old - aiming to follow in the footsteps of compatriot Collin Morikawa, who won the Race to Dubai in 2021 - is around 300 points clear of McIlroy with five DP World Tour events remaining. How were the European champions not a shoo-in for the next major tournament in the international calendar? The Lionesses only missed out by a whisker, finishing their qualifying campaign with 15 points from a possible 18. Just one result away. But it's difficult to overlook how we got here. England's 4-0 defeat to Spain was an eye-opener, their biggest margin of loss for 17 years. The heaviest of Sarina Wiegman's time in charge. It highlighted a gulf that felt more technical than tactical. In the moment, Spain showed themselves to be streets ahead in style and substance. A team with a plan, rooted in DNA and identity. metadata.summary: Lionel Messi described playing for Argentina as "the most wonderful thing that can happen to you" after ending his international career with a goal in a 3-0 win over Benin in Buenos Aires.
metadata.content: Lionel Messi ends Argentina career with goal and two assists against Benin on emotional night | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lionel Messi ends Argentina career with goal and two assists against Benin on emotional night Lionel Messi finishes his international career with 208 senior caps, the most of any player in the team's history, with his 126 goals for Argentina also a record; On an emotional night against Benin, Messi also created the first two goals, before getting on the scoresheet himself Wednesday 7 October 2026 09:35, UK Lionel Messi described playing for Argentina as "the most wonderful thing that can happen to you" after ending his international career with a goal in a 3-0 win over Benin in Buenos Aires. The 39-year-old ends his international career with 208 senior caps, the most of any player in the team's history, with his 126 goals for Argentina also a record. Messi won the 2022 World Cup and two Copa Americas during his 21-year spell on the international stage. David Croft has questioned the FIA after the chaotic formation lap scenes at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, describing a software glitch that saw several drivers slowing to a crawl or stopping completely as a "farce". F1 and the FIA have new technical regulations this year which saw the introduction of a new power unit which is almost 50 per cent electric. Sepang saw the first wet conditions of the season, and the FIA later confirmed that a combination of low engine speeds, low grip, wet-weather energy-management settings and the configuration of the circuit had caused an unintended loss of power.
